messages:
marcus: Heads-up — noticed a steady increase in evictions and pending tiny-gpu pods in ap-southeast1 over the last 3 hours. Cluster-wide GPU allocs fragmented; warm nodes not being reused.

sam: saw that too. 20-30 small pods pending, binpack score bouncing. Can repro with `kubectl get pods -A | grep Pending`.

vlad: any network blips or attach/detach errors in the node logs? those often cause attach latency and lead to latebind eviction chains.

marcus: dug into kubelet and kube-scheduler logs: lots of AttachVolume timeout + preempt rebinds. snippet: ```
I0315 12:08:42.123 kubelet.go:1234] attach timeout for volume vol-gpu-warm: rpc deadline exceeded
I0315 12:08:42.456 scheduler.go:987] preempt chain triggered for pod ml-train-small-xyz, moved -> pending on node drift-005
```

maria: opsbot reported a spike in descheduler runs at 12:05 too, maybe trying to rebalance but it’s making tiny-pod churn worse.

opsbot: deploybot: descheduler v2.1 rolled at 12:00 to ap-southeast1 (canary). Config: backfill=true, preferLargest=false.

sam: preferLargest=false might be doing the wrong thing for our workload. small pods get pulled out of warm nodes instead of consolidated.

vlad: agree. packing policy should prefer filling big-gpus first. Can we flip `preferLargest=true` in canary?

marcus: we could also temporarily relax anti-affinity for low-priority tiny jobs to allow coalescing on fewer nodes. downside: potential NVLINK saturation for some users.

maria: cost impact note: consolidation reduces node-hours -> saves ~6-8% on GPU reserved hourly spend in that region during spikes. But we need to measure latency tail for jobs that rely on intra-node comms.

sam: proposed immediate action: 1) revert canary descheduler config to preferLargest=true 2) run a one-off descheduler job that evicts small non-critical pods into consolidated nodes 3) enable a short-lived feature-flag `allow-smallpod-coalesce` for low-priority namespaces. Thoughts?

vlad: +1 on (1). For (2) we should scope to namespaces `test-ml` and `batch-internal` only. And include a dry-run first.

marcus: @oncall-bot can you run `kubectl apply -f descheduler-preferlargest.yaml` to the canary control plane? patch will be: `spec.strategy: \"RemoveDuplicates\"` + `preferLargest: true`.

oncall-bot: ack I will run it in 5m and post results.

maria: caution — if we coalesce too aggressively, we may create a hotspot for NVLINK/PCIe and cause perf regressions. Add a telemetry gate: if p95 latency of infra models increases >10% we auto-rollback.

sam: good call. I'll add a kpis job to watch p95 token latency and GPU utilization.

vlad: while we toggle, can platform team increase warmnode threshold TTL to avoid warm nodes being reclaimed too fast? Current TTL is 300s. bump to 900s might reduce churn.

marcus: agreed. Action list:
- sam: run canary descheduler revert and one-off dry-run evict for scoped namespaces (ETA 10m)
- vlad: open quick patch to warmnode-controller TTL -> 900s, roll in 30m
- maria: add telemetry gate (p95 latency + nvlink errs) and hook to rollback automation
- oncall-bot: monitor eviction rate and post summary in 15m

sam: starting now — will post dry-run output.

oncall-bot: descheduler patch applied to canary at 12:20. dry-run evict returned 34 candidate pods (namespaces: test-ml, batch-internal).

maria: starting telemetry watchers. hooking into infra-metrics-alerts.

vlad: PR for TTL bump opened: https://git.company/repo/pull/432 — small rollout (canary on ap-southeast1 only).

marcus: quick note — while this helps consolidation, we should schedule a deeper postmortem: cause of AttachVolume timeouts. If that's solved, churn likely stops. Filing short incident ticket.

maria: thanks. I'll add cost delta estimate once we see consolidation stabilized.

sam: dry-run results look promising. On live run we'll evict in waves of 20 to avoid overload. scheduling now in 2m.

oncall-bot: live eviction wave 1 started at 12:27. 20 pods evicted, 18 rescheduled onto 6 warm nodes.

marcus: keeping an eye. ping me if p95 token latency > +8%.

maria: p95 is stable so far (+2%), GPU util on consolidated nodes increased from 35%->62%.

vlad: rolling TTL bump to 900s in canary now.

sam: wave 2 will run in 10m if metrics OK.

oncall-bot: eviction rate dropped by 40% vs baseline after wave 1.

marcus: nice. follow-up chores: incident ticket w/ timeline, add test to verify descheduler preferLargest default, add runbook entry for `allow-smallpod-coalesce` flag and thresholds.

maria: assigning tasks. I'll own incident ticket and cost calc.

vlad: I'll own warmnode-controller PR and perf follow-up for NVLINK hotspots.

sam: I'll add rollback playbook and add the canary to the scheduler-runbooks page.

marcus: thanks team. close loop in 24h with postmortem. :thumbsup:
